added_lines: . a victory for the generations what an extraordinary few days it has been for durrow and cullohill! the celebrations following the historic victory last sunday will live long in the memories of everyone associated with the club and our two communities. and deservedly so. sixty-two years after cullohill’s great win and forty-two years since the harps was formed, the dream of winning a senior county championship has finally been realised. but amidst all the excitement and celebrations, i found myself thinking about another group of people: those who would have loved to see this day but are no longer with us. a few weeks ago, while working with priests in mayo, i was struck by how often people spoke about their county's great all-ireland victory, not simply in terms of the present generation, but of parents, grandparents and generations of supporters who had gone before them. people who followed their team through good times and bad, who dreamed of such a day but never lived to see it. i suspect there were similar thoughts in many hearts and homes around durrow and cullohill last sunday. how many former players, parents, grandparents and lifelong supporters would have given anything to witness that final whistle? some now have sons, grandsons or even great-grandsons among this extraordinary group of young men. their contribution to sunday's victory may not appear in any match report, but surely it is part of the story. as we approach november, the month when we traditionally remember our dead, there is something particularly appropriate this year about remembering those who helped build and sustain the clubs down through the generations. we inherit far more than a name or a place. we inherit traditions, loyalties, friendships and dreams. sometimes, without even realising it, we find ourselves completing something that others began long before us. this sunday's gospel reminds us of the great commandment to love god and to love our neighbour. perhaps one of the loveliest expressions of that love is the sense of community, belonging and generosity that occasions like last sunday bring to the surface. despite my camross roots, and the shock and disappointment being felt in the foothills of the sliabh blooms, seeing the joy this victory has brought to the people among whom i now live and serve has been something very special indeed. so, congratulations to every member of the harps family. enjoy this wonderful achievement. and somewhere in the celebrations, spare a thought for those who would have loved to be there. this victory belongs to them too. fr. martin christmas concert michael english, featuring durrow and cullohill parish choirs sunday 6th december 2026 in holy trinity church, durrow. doors open at 5 pm for 6 pm start. a festive evening of songs, stories, faith & inspiration tickets €30 available from both of our parish ofïces (opening times below) or through

this world mission sunday marks the 100th anniversary of its establishment by pope pius xi in 1926. this centenary is an opportunity to celebrate with renewed m issionary zeal. last year, pope leo xiv made an appeal to us in a personal video for world mission sunday. his request echoed around t he world: “please help me help missionaries everywhere.” that’s what world mission sunday does: it helps pope leo care for the 1,130 missionary dioceses and territories under his supervision through the dicastery for evangelization. we are all called to be a part of this missionary work, and we have a singular means to do so: world mission sunday. the second collection we take up today helps extend the church’s evangelisation work to missionary lands where the gospel is being proclaimed for the first time, as well as to places where the church barely exists, or is too young, too persecuted, or to sustain herself. thank you for responding to pope leo’s call to help him help missio naries everywhere! “what does god want from the church in ireland at this time?” the working document for the irish national synodal assembly, which took p lace in gormanston, co. meath, on saturday 17th october 2026, has been published. entitled “is not this what god asks of you?” the document brings together the fru its of five years of prayer, listening and discernment along the irish synodal pathway. it formed the basis for the prayer, conversation, discernment and deliberation of delegates as they p articipated in the national synodal assembly on saturday. but this is not a document for assembly delegates only. the working document belongs within the wider journey of the irish synodal pathway and reflects the voices, hopes, concerns and discernment of people and communities from across the church in ireland. we therefore invite everyone to read it, pray with it and reflect on the question th at has accompanied the synodal pathway from the beginning. visit

prayers for pope leo many of us were moved last sunday when pope leo shared, simply and calmly , that doctors had found a small growth on his lung. on tuesday he had surgery at rome’s gemelli hospital, where part of his right lung was removed. the vatican has since confirmed it was an early-stage lung cancer, and that the operation went well, withou t complications. he is expected to rest in hospital for about a week, his audiences have been cancelled until 20th october, and he still hopes to make his journey to south america in november. let us pray for our holy father this week, along with everyone in our own parish facing illness and treatment. lord jesus, divine healer, we place our holy father, pope leo, in your loving care. guide the hands of his doctors and nurses, grant him rest, strength and peace, and restore him to full health, that he may continue to shepherd your people with joy. mary, health of the sick, pray for him. amen. taizé youth programme 2027 a youth trip to taizé in france organised by ossory youth will take place from sunday, 27th june to sunday, 4th july 2027. a week in the taizé community is an opportunity for reflection and contemplation and a little step back from daily life. however, bringing people together is also the essence of taizé and it is a week of meeting young people from different countries and cultures where new friendships are made. tens of tho usands of young people from around the world, including 25 from kilkenny, will made the trip to taizé next year. the programme, which runs from november 2026 to july 2027 is open to transition year and 5th year students. closing date for applications is friday, 6th november. for additional information, including cost and application forms, contact patrick bookle, ossory youth at
